title: European Commission confirms 'AI-generated' cyber campaign, took applications offline
date_note: Published November 19 (Thursday); the Commission says the campaign was detected on October 22.
summary: According to Newsweek, Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said the Commission was the target of an 'AI-generated' cybercampaign by an unknown individual or group, detected on October 22. The Commission temporarily took down several applications, and most have since been restored. The investigation is ongoing.
plain: The European Commission says it was hit by a cyberattack that it describes as AI-generated, and briefly took some systems offline.
exec: A government body reports AI-assisted attack activity; attacker identity and impact are not yet public.
impact: Several applications temporarily taken down, most restored (Newsweek quoting the Commission).

validation.note: Newsweek quotes a Commission spokesperson; MSN version returned no text; Commission statement itself not opened. Newsweek text carries no explicit date.
